Bloodwork

Every drug card and calculator uses this weight.

Welcome

One rule, every drug

Bloodwork is built around a single idea, and everything else grows out of it: percent means grams in every hundred millilitres. Once that sits comfortably, every dilution, every drip and every drug calculation turns into the same handful of moves, which you'll find laid out step by step under Learn, turned into reflex under Games, tested under Test Prep, and applied to every drug in the library, where the dose calculator runs live against whatever patient weight you set.

Clock

How fast do you want to be?

Timed questions are what turn knowing into reflex, so pick a clock you can live with for now and tighten it as you improve. Thirty seconds is a fair place to start.

Patient

Default weight

Every drug card doses against one patient weight, and you can change it any time from the chip in the top corner, so set a sensible default here.

Daily

Ten minutes a day

Twelve minutes a day is the whole plan. The Dashboard lines up five short things: flash cards that resurface right before you'd forget them, a quick quiz aimed at whatever you've been missing, a drug check, one scenario step and one drug exercise. Finish all five and the day goes green; do anything at all and it goes yellow. XP from every round feeds your level and badges.

Mnemonics, sayings and rules of thumb. Search anything, filter by category, and tap a card to see what it stands for and why it matters.

Games

Build the foundations

Short rounds, one skill each, grouped by what they build. Every round earns XP toward your level, and each category ring grades from bronze to master as you keep playing. Drug Exercises is the long game; the rest are quick.

Drug Exercises

Learn a drug

Five lessons per drug: identify it, know when it is used, type the adult doses, then the pediatric doses and timing, then a checkpoint. Miss one and it comes back before the round ends. The list keeps what you are working on first, then your starred study set.

Registry simulator

Practice tests

Paper tests with an answer key

Generate a fresh test and print it from the installed app, or copy it as text into a document. Lane cards from Scenarios land here as well.

Every WVFD profile, searchable by name, brand, class or indication. Open a card for the full mechanism and the dosages, grouped by route and worked for the patient weight in the header, with the standard bag for anything that runs as a drip.

Source: WVFD Drug Profiles, based on AHA, ACLS and PALS common practice with AZDHS and JB Learning content. Training reference. Verify against your current protocol.
